endorsements.quote: To ensure purpose, the VA will assess patient and clinician needs and design AI that targets meaningful problems to avoid scope creep or feature bloat.
The VA will establish oversight processes to quickly identify any declines in reliability or unfair impacts on subgroups.
Codesign AI transparency features with end users.
They will proactively assess datasets and algorithms for potential biases based on protected attributes like race, gender, or age.
Biased outputs will be addressed through techniques such as data augmentation, reweighting, and algorithm tweaks.
Technical controls will prevent unauthorized access or changes to AI systems.
Audits will check for appropriate internal usage per policies.
Continual patches and upgrades will maintain security.
Documentation will detail an AI system’s data sources, methodology, testing, limitations, and integration with clinical workflows.
Clinicians and patients will receive education on interpreting AI outputs.

unlisted_practices: Build security into the AI development process.
Leaders should communicate the importance of responsible AI through words and actions.
Use culture surveys to assess baseline awareness of AI ethics issues and target education.
Retrain AI models as needed based on incoming data patterns.
Incorporate veteran and patient perspectives on AI through participatory design and advisory councils.
Track metrics such as explainability and bias on dashboards.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/framework paper describing the implementation of trustworthy AI in the VA using high reliability health care principles and the VA National AI Institute's Trustworthy AI Framework.
